6550.stem:
The network diagram shows tasks that must be completed to finish a project. Each edge weight represents the time taken to complete the task, in days.

\exfigure{819_q32_1}

figures.cap: project activity network A to K

parts.latex: What is the earliest start time (EST) of activity $H$?
What is minimum completion time for the project?
What is the critical path for the project?
What is the float time of activity $E$?

solutions.latex:
Activity $H$ starts after $E$, $F$ and $G$ are all finished, so its EST is the longest of the paths into the node where they meet.
$$\begin{aligned} A,F &: 3+7=10 \\ B,E &: 2+5=7 \\ B,C,D,G &: 2+4+3+5=14 \end{aligned}$$
The longest is 14 days.
$$\therefore\ \text{EST of } H = 14 \text{ days}$$
criteria: Finds the length of at least two paths into the start of $H$, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Checked all three paths into node before H.

solutions.latex:
After $H$ and $I$, $J$, the finish of the project needs $K$. The activity $K$ starts when both $H$ and $J$ are complete.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{via } H &: 14+4=18 \\ \text{via } I,J &: 14+2+4=20 \end{aligned}$$
So $K$ starts at day 20 and takes 3 days.
$$\therefore\ \text{minimum completion time} = 20+3 = 23 \text{ days}$$

The critical path is the longest path from start to finish, with length 23 days.

The longest route to the node before $H$ and $I$ is $B,C,D,G$ (14 days). After that, $I,J$ (6 days) is longer than $H$ (4 days).
$$\begin{aligned} B+C+D+G+I+J+K &= 2+4+3+5+2+4+3 \\ &= 23 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{critical path: } B,C,D,G,I,J,K$$
criteria: Identifies a path of length 23 incompletely, or finds the longest route to the node before $H$, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Sum of path = 23 = minimum completion time.

solutions.latex:
Float time $=$ LST $-$ EST, or equivalently (latest finish) $-$ (EST) $-$ (duration).

$E$ starts after $B$, so its EST is 2 days. It must finish by day 14, the EST of $H$ and $I$ (the critical path reaches that node at day 14).
$$\begin{aligned} \text{float} &= 14-2-5 \\ &= 7 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{float time of } E = 7 \text{ days}$$

parts.latex: List the activities that make up the critical path and give the minimum time required to complete the manufacturing process.

The foreman is told that one activity has been delayed by 10 minutes, but he is not concerned, as it will not delay the whole process.

Which possible activities could he have been told about?

solutions.latex:
Label the nodes: $P$ (end of $A$), $Q$ (end of $C$), $R$ (end of $E$, $B$, $F$), $S$ (end of $G$, $H$). Find the earliest start time at each node, taking the longest route.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 12 \\ Q &= 14 \\ R &= \max(12+10,\ 15,\ 14+13) = 27 \\ S &= \max(27+12,\ 14+20) = 39 \\ \text{End} &= \max(12+25,\ 39+12) = 51 \end{aligned}$$
The longest route is $C \to F \to H \to I$:
$$\begin{aligned} 14+13+12+12 &= 51 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Critical path: } C,\ F,\ H,\ I; \text{ minimum time } 51 \text{ minutes.}$$
criteria: Correct critical path with an incorrect time, or equivalent merit
Finds earliest start times or a path of long duration, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Enumerated all paths: A-D 37, A-E-H-I 46, B-H-I 39, C-F-H-I 51, C-G-I 46. Max 51.
meta.generated_note: Generated worked solution. Network read from figure: A: start-P, B: start-R, C: start-Q, D: P-end, E: P-R, F: Q-R, G: Q-S, H: R-S, I: S-end.

solutions.latex:
A delay of 10 minutes does not delay the process only if the activity has float of at least 10 minutes.

Compare each non-critical activity's float (latest finish minus earliest start minus duration), using the longest path through it:

More simply, compare the longest path through each activity with 51 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} A,\ E,\ H,\ I &: 12+10+12+12 = 46 \text{ (float } 5\text{)} \\ B,\ H,\ I &: 15+12+12 = 39 \text{ (float } 12\text{)} \\ A,\ D &: 12+25 = 37 \text{ (float } 14\text{)} \\ C,\ G,\ I &: 14+20+12 = 46 \text{ (float } 5\text{)} \end{aligned}$$
Activities $A$, $E$ and $G$ lie on a path of 46 minutes, so a 10 minute delay would make the process 5 minutes longer. $A$ is also on path $A,D$ but its longest path is 46, so its float is 5.

Only $B$ (float 12) and $D$ (float 14) can absorb a delay of 10 minutes.
$$\therefore\ \text{He could have been told about activity } B \text{ or activity } D.$$
criteria: Finds the float of the non-critical activities, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Computed float by earliest/latest times: A 5, B 12, D 14, E 5, G 5, critical C, F, H, I 0.

The foreman is told that one activity has been delayed by 10 minutes, but he is not concerned, as it will not delay the whole process.

Which are the three possible activities that will not delay the whole process?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1264_q31_s1}

The critical path is the longest path through the network, found from the forward and backward scans.
$$\text{Critical path: } C \text{ then } F \text{ then } H \text{ then } I$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Minimum time} = 51 \text{ minutes}$$
criteria: Forward and backward scans, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
An activity can be delayed without delaying the whole process if its float time is at least $10$ minutes.

Activities $A$ and $D$ have float times of $14$ minutes, and $B$ has a float time of $12$ minutes.
$$\therefore\ A,\ B \text{ and } D \text{ could be delayed}$$
